The Trichy assault rifle (TAR), sometimes known as the Tiruchi assault rifle, is an Indian-made assault rifle chambered for the 7.62×39mm round. It was developed by the Ordnance Factory in Tiruchirappalli and is designed to destroy the enemy by fire in single and burst firing modes. The TAR is a powerful automatic weapon, similar to the AK-47 in design and capability. It has been procured by various Indian security forces, including the Border Security Force (BSF) and the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), enhancing their firepower. The TAR has an effective range of 400 meters and is equipped with a bayonet. It has been praised for its reliability and performance in various field trials.

The Trichy assault rifle is a significant development in Indian military equipment, providing a domestically produced alternative to imported assault rifles. Its chambering of the 7.62x39mm round allows it to utilize a wider range of ammunition and accessories, making it a versatile weapon for different combat scenarios.

2.content:
**Demand of TAR among Central Reserved Forces**

TAR or Trichy Assault Rifle is a product from erstwhile Ordinance Factory Trichy and now part of AWEIL. The development of the assault rifle was started in 2015 and a production line was established in 2017. The first batch of 200 TARs were delivered to Chandigarh police in March 2017. In November 2017, the CRPF tested the rifle’s functionality and its reliability. Over 15,000 rounds were fired to test the TAR’s life cycle and over 2,400 rounds to test its reliability. In February 2018, the TAR underwent field trial at Jagdalpur, Raipur, Guwahati and Srinagar. After regressive trials, the CRPF had placed an order for 6167 rifles TAR.

In January 2024, it was reported that BSF is acquiring 125 TAR rifles along with bayonets and other accessories. BSF has experience with operating TAR and has inducted the assault rifle into service earlier. Other Central Armed Police Forces which include SSB, ITBP & CISF has also procured TAR in some significant numbers. Police forces in several states have also inducted TAR under their modernisation scheme.

**TAR : Specifications**

The Trichy Assault Rifle (TAR) is a 7.62X39mm powerful automatic weapon designed to destroy the enemy by fire in single and burst firing mode. It has an effective range of 350m. Its light weight and modular design make it suitable for the counter-insurgency and counter-terror operations. It comes with foldable and fixed butt type, depending upon the requirement. The foldable butt version is helpful in quick and easy movement of personnel in guard and patrolling duty. The overall length of TAR-Down folding butt is 900mm in butt open condition and 650mm in butt folding condition. The rifle weighs 3.4kg and features a curved magazine with 30 rounds.

The rifle has mono-block receiver body & fibre reinforced polymer magazine with steel inserts. It also has a customised version with single round firing mode for police forces. It also features Tritium filled Sources for night firing and picatinny rail for mounting optical sights. It can also be fitted with Under barrel grenade launcher.

TAR very closely resembles Bulgarian Arsenal AR-M1F41. There is minor difference in the gas block & cleaning rod of the assault rifles. There is also some noticeable difference in the pistol grip. TAR is being supplied to paramilitary forces to reduce imports from Bulgaria. The unique feature of TAR is that it provides 12 O’clock rails on upper handguard which is not available in any other AKM copy. TAR is 7.62x39mm assault rifle, similar in calibre to AK-203. In fact TAR is almost equivalent to AK-103 and very close to AK-203 in terms of performance.

Launch of 7.62*39mm Trichy Assault Rifle (TAR) Down Folding Butt Version
------------------------------------------------------------------------

 प्रविष्टि तिथि: 26 AUG 2021 12:51PM by PIB Chennai 

In commemoration of 75 years of independence, Ordnance Factory, Tiruchirappalli launched Down folding butt version of 7.62*39mm Trichy Assault Rifle on 25 th August 2021. At present, Ordnance Factory, Tiruchirappali, is manufacturing TAR Rifles in two variants i.e. Fixed butt and side folding butt versions.

The 7.62*39mm Trichy Assault Rifle (TAR) is a powerful individual automatic weapon designed to destroy the enemy by fire in single and burst firing mode. It is a single shot Rifle in normal mode and it can be used in burst mode also. By firing in burst mode in short series, group or single targets at a range up to 500m can be destroyed. However, the destructive effect of the TAR is up to a range of 1350m.

Ordnance Factory, Trichirappallin developed and manufactured TAR Down folding butt version to meet the customer requirement as some of the CAPF units, State Police and RPF required the Down folding butt version for quick and easy movement of personnel in guard and patrolling duty.

The overall length of TAR-Down folding butt is 900mm in butt open condition and 650mm in butt folding condition.

The Down folding butt version of 7.62*39mm Trichy Assault Rifle launched by Shri Sanjay Dwivedi, IOFS, General Manager, Ordnance Factory, Trichirappalli and Shri Rajiv Jain, IOFS, Addl. Times of India [reports](http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2011-03-19/india/29145725_1_ordnance-factory-happ-tiruchi) …

> TIRUCHI: The Ordnance Factory of Tiruchi (OFT) has designed and developed an indigenous assault rifle matching the specifications of the AK47.
> 
> 
> “When put into use by our armed forces and other security agencies, the rifle will be recognized as pride of India. Ordnance Factory Tiruchy (OFT) in March 2020 handed over the first consignment of 500 assault rifles to CRPF. Trichy Assault Rifles or TAR, as these are called, are the indigenous version of AK-47 rifle. Shirish Khare, GM, OFT handed over the rifles to DS Rawat, DIG, CRPF. OFT started the development of the rifle in 2015, and established a production line in 2017. The first batch of 200 TARs was delivered to Chandigarh police in March 2017. In November 2017, the CRPF tested the rifle for functionality and reliability. It was subjected to a life cycle test by firing 15,000 rounds in one go. In February 2018, the TAR was deployed for a field trial at Jagdalpur, Raipur, Guwahati and Srinagar. Following this, order for 6167 rifles were placed. OFT would supply TARs in both fixed and foldable butt models, sources said adding that the latter was in the development stage. The TAR is compatible with GP-25, 30 and UBGL M-6 grenade launchers. OFT has so far supplied more than 10,000 rifles to Central Armed Police Forces including the BSF, SSB, ITBP & CISF. Police force in several States have also inducted TAR under their modernisation scheme. OFT has also taken up research and development projects such as the trial of 7.62X39mm TAR Carbine(long barrel firearm) and 40X46mm UBGL (Underbarrel Grenade Launcher) for TAR/AK 47, which after induction would serve as an import substitute. The TAR, which is made of solid metal, is also fundamentally said to be sturdier than the AK-203, which is made of sheet metal. TAR being suppled to paramilitary forces, and is set to replace imports from Bulgaria. TAR dubbed to be at par with Kalashnikov in terms of functionality. Over 15,000 rounds were fired to test the TAR’s life cycle and over 2,400 for reliability. The trials were carried out at the CRPF Academy. Earlier, the Army had preferred the 5.56mm ammunition going by the theory that an injured enemy is of more use than a dead one. In November 2017, the CRPF tested the rifle for functionality and reliability. It was subjected to a life cycle test by firing 15,000 rounds in one go. In February 2018, the TAR was deployed for a field trial at Jagdalpur, Raipur, Guwahati and Srinagar. Following this, order for 6167 rifles were placed. OFT would supply TARs in both fixed and foldable butt models, sources said adding that the latter was in the development stage. The TAR is compatible with GP-25, 30 and UBGL M-6 grenade launchers. OFT has so far supplied more than 10,000 rifles to Central Armed Police Forces including the BSF, SSB, ITBP & CISF. Police force in several States have also inducted TAR under their modernisation scheme.
